items.stem: The fundamental insurance ratemaking equation states that the rate should cover:

options.text: Expected losses, expenses and a provision for profit/contingencies
options.rationale: Correct: rates fund losses, expenses and a profit/contingency load.

options.text: Only paid losses from last month
options.rationale: Rates are prospective and must cover expenses and profit too.
Investment income is one consideration, not the whole rate.
Competitor pricing is a business factor, not the actuarial equation.

items.explanation: Correct: rates fund losses, expenses and a profit/contingency load.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An exposure base for ratemaking should ideally be:

options.text: Proportional to expected loss and practical to measure
options.rationale: Correct: a good exposure base varies with risk and is easy to administer.

options.text: Unrelated to the risk being insured
options.rationale: An unrelated base fails to track loss potential.
Auditability is a desirable, not undesirable, property.
A constant base cannot differentiate risk.

items.explanation: Correct: a good exposure base varies with risk and is easy to administer.

items.stem: Select TWO methods commonly used to estimate unpaid claim liabilities.

options.rationale: Correct: chain-ladder develops losses to ultimate using development factors.
Correct: Bornhuetter-Ferguson blends expected losses with reported development.

options.text: Choosing the reserve that matches the budget target
options.rationale: Reserves are estimated from data, not set to hit a budget.

options.text: Using the CEO’s preferred round number
options.rationale: Reserve estimation is actuarial, not arbitrary.

options.text: Ignoring development of recent accident years
options.rationale: Recent years need development; ignoring it understates reserves.

items.explanation: Correct: chain-ladder develops losses to ultimate using development factors.
